She is pushed by the Dorothy Ann, a 7,200-horsepower Z-drive tug.

vessels.name: ST MARYS CHALLENGER
vessels.fact: Hull dates to 1906 — cut down to a cement barge in 2014
vessels.source: Wikipedia SS St. Marys Challenger; professionalmariner.com 2014. SUPERLATIVE SOFTENED — she was the oldest operating self-propelled laker, a title that lapsed at conversion. NOTE: 552 ft is as-built; Wikipedia gives 527 ft as the shortened barge length.
facts: Hull dates to 1906 — cut down to a cement barge in 2014
Before her 2014 refit she was the oldest operating freighter on the Great Lakes.
A rare Skinner Unaflow steam engine made her one of the last lakes steamships.
She began life in 1906 as the ore carrier William P. Snyder.
Her pilothouse is now preserved at the National Museum of the Great Lakes.

vessels.name: ST MARYS CONQUEST
vessels.fact: Born 1937 as the oil tanker Red Crown — now hauls cement
vessels.source: greatlakesships.wordpress.com/red-crown — built 1937 by Manitowoc for Standard Oil of Indiana as tanker Red Crown; barge conversion 1987. LENGTH CORRECTED: 465 ft was as-built; 437 ft 6 in after the 1992 rebuild.
facts: Born 1937 as the oil tanker Red Crown — now hauls cement
She spent her first half-century hauling petroleum for Standard Oil and Amoco.
Manitowoc Shipbuilding launched her into the Manitowoc River in 1937.
From Red Crown to St. Marys Conquest, she has carried a whole string of names.

vessels.name: USCGC MACKINAW
vessels.fact: Great Lakes heavy icebreaker — replaced the 1944 Mackinaw
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Mackinaw_(WLBB-30)
facts: Great Lakes heavy icebreaker — replaced the 1944 Mackinaw
She steers with two rotating Azipod thrusters and carries no rudder at all.
Besides breaking heavy ice she doubles as a Great Lakes buoy tender.
Marinette Marine in Wisconsin built her; Cheboygan, Michigan is her home port.

vessels.name: CGC HOLLYHOCK
vessels.fact: 225-ft buoy tender and icebreaker — left the Lakes in 2023
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Hollyhock_(WLB-214)
facts: 225-ft buoy tender and icebreaker — left the Lakes in 2023
She is named for an earlier Coast Guard Hollyhock that served from 1937 to 1982.
A Juniper-class buoy tender, she was built at Marinette, Wisconsin in 2003.

vessels.name: CGC ALDER
vessels.fact: The last Juniper-class buoy tender ever built — launched 2004
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Alder_(WLB-216)
facts: The last Juniper-class buoy tender ever built — launched 2004
She replaced the cutter Sundew, which had served the Coast Guard for sixty years.
She was built by Marinette Marine in Wisconsin and long homeported at Duluth, Minnesota.
In 2022 she left the Great Lakes for a new posting in San Francisco Bay.

vessels.name: CGC BISCAYNE BAY
vessels.fact: Homeported at St. Ignace since 1979 — the bridge's own icebreaker
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Biscayne_Bay
facts: Homeported at St. Ignace since 1979 — the bridge's own icebreaker
She's named after Biscayne Bay in Florida, just off the city of Miami.
She was built far away in Tacoma, Washington, on the Pacific coast.
She's the fourth of the Coast Guard's nine 140-foot Bay-class cutters.
She can push through twenty inches of ice at a steady continuous speed.

vessels.name: CGC NEAH BAY
vessels.fact: Blows air bubbles under her hull to slip through thick ice
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Neah_Bay
facts: Blows air bubbles under her hull to slip through thick ice
She's named after Neah Bay, at the far northwest corner of Washington State.
She's homeported in Cleveland, keeping Lake Erie's shipping channels open in winter.
She was built in Tacoma, Washington, and launched in February 1980.
She has even carried a rescued Himalayan cat named Casca as ship's mascot.

vessels.name: CGC KATMAI BAY
vessels.fact: Lead ship of the Bay class — first of nine, Soo-based since 1979
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Katmai_Bay
facts: Lead ship of the Bay class — first of nine, Soo-based since 1979
She's named after Katmai Bay in Alaska's Katmai National Park, famous for its brown bears.
She works hand in hand with the far larger icebreaker Mackinaw.
She was built in Tacoma, Washington, and can make nearly fifteen knots.
In 2018 she underwent a major service-life extension refit at the Coast Guard's Baltimore shipyard.

vessels.name: CGC MOBILE BAY
vessels.fact: Breaks 27 inches of ice at 3 knots — Sturgeon Bay's icebreaker
vessels.source: https://www.atlanticarea.uscg.mil/Our-Organization/District-9/Ninth-District-Staff/Prevention-Division/Cutters/MOBILE-BAY/Characteristics/
facts: Breaks 27 inches of ice at 3 knots — Sturgeon Bay's icebreaker
She's named after Mobile Bay in Alabama, on the Gulf of Mexico.
She sails with her own 120-foot buoy barge to tend navigation aids on the Great Lakes.
She's the third of the Coast Guard's nine Bay-class icebreaking tugs.

vessels.name: CGC BRISTOL BAY
vessels.fact: Sails with her own 120-ft buoy barge, mated back in 1991
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Bristol_Bay
facts: Sails with her own 120-ft buoy barge, mated back in 1991
She's named after Bristol Bay in Alaska, one of the world's great salmon fisheries.
She's homeported in Detroit, watching over the busy Detroit River.
She was the second Bay-class cutter ever built, back in 1978.
Her buoy barge helps her tend over 160 navigation aids each year.

vessels.name: PRIME
vessels.fact: A Norwegian ocean tanker — one of the 'salties' that reach the Lakes from the Atlantic through the St. Lawrence Seaway, rarer here than the home-fleet lakers
vessels.source: vesselfinder.com IMO 9267558 — chemical/oil products tanker, Norway flag, 140 m LOA, 14,750 DWT, mgr OSM Ship Management
facts: A Norwegian ocean tanker — one of the 'salties' that reach the Lakes from the Atlantic through the St. Lawrence Seaway, rarer here than the home-fleet lakers
She's a chemical and oil-products tanker, stretching about 460 feet long.
She can carry close to fifteen thousand tonnes of liquid cargo.

vessels.name: VIKING POLARIS
vessels.fact: Carries two six-passenger submarines — built 2022 for polar ice
vessels.source: https://www.vard.com/shipbuilding/references/viking-polaris
facts: Carries two six-passenger submarines — built 2022 for polar ice
Her godmother is Ann Bancroft, the first woman to trek to both Poles.
Her identical twin sister ship is the Viking Octantis.
Norway's VARD shipyard built her, and she stretches some 665 feet long.
Beyond polar seas, she's designed to explore North America's Great Lakes.

vessels.name: LE CHAMPLAIN
vessels.fact: Has 'Blue Eye' — a lounge with windows below the waterline
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Champlain
facts: Has 'Blue Eye' — a lounge with windows below the waterline
She's named for Samuel de Champlain, the explorer called the Father of New France.
One of six Ponant sisters, each named for a famous French explorer.
She carries just 180 guests for intimate, small-ship expedition cruising.
Her hull was built in Romania, then finished in Norway.

vessels.name: JOHN D LEITCH
vessels.fact: Sailing since 1967 — rebuilt in 2002 and renamed John D. Leitch
vessels.source: https://www.boatnerd.com/pictures/fleet/JohnDLeitch.htm
facts: Sailing since 1967 — rebuilt in 2002 and renamed John D. Leitch
She was built in 1967 as the Canadian Century at Ontario's Port Weller Dry Docks.
She's named for John D. Leitch, longtime chairman of Upper Lakes Shipping.
Algoma Central added her to its Great Lakes fleet in 2011.

vessels.name: RADCLIFFE R LATIMER
vessels.fact: Rebuilt in China 2008-09 — sailed as Algobay until renamed 2012
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radcliffe_R._Latimer — LENGTH CORRECTED: 730ft was the pre-rebuild figure; the 2009 China rebuild took LOA to 741ft 10in. Renamed 4 Oct 2012 for a former Algoma Central board chairman.
facts: Rebuilt in China 2008-09 — sailed as Algobay until renamed 2012
She is named for Radcliffe Latimer, a former chairman of Algoma Central.
She was built in 1978 by Collingwood Shipbuilding in Collingwood, Ontario.
She was built to serve a fifteen-year contract hauling about a million tonnes of coal a year for Ontario Hydro.

vessels.name: TIM MCKEIL
vessels.fact: Built in Japan in 1991 to serve Australian iron ore ports
vessels.source: https://gltugs.wordpress.com/tim-mckeil/ — built 1991 by Matsuura Tekko Zosen, Higashino, Japan as Pannawonica I for Cleveland Cliffs-Robe River Iron (Australia). LENGTH CORRECTED 105 -> 107ft 09in. Single-source.
facts: Built in Japan in 1991 to serve Australian iron ore ports
She was built in Japan in 1991 as the Pannawonica I for an Australian iron-ore company.
She is a powerful twin-screw z-drive tractor tug rated at 4,800 horsepower.
McKeil Marine of Hamilton, Ontario acquired and renamed her in 2014.

vessels.name: JARRETT M
vessels.fact: Built 1945 in Owen Sound, Ontario as the tug Atomic
vessels.source: https://gltugs.wordpress.com/jarrett-m/ — built 1945 by Russel Brothers Ltd, Owen Sound, as Atomic; still active for McKeil. LENGTH CORRECTED 80.5 -> 82ft. Dropped '80 years on the towline' — it is 81 years as of 2026 and the number goes stale.
facts: Built 1945 in Owen Sound, Ontario as the tug Atomic
She was designed as an icebreaker able to crack ice up to thirty inches thick.
She was built in 1945 by the renowned Russel Brothers tug works for McQueen Marine of Amherstburg.
She was renamed Jarrett M in 2007, after more than sixty years of service.

vessels.name: VICTORIOUS
vessels.fact: China-built 2009 ATB tug — 5,384 hp pushing heated asphalt
vessels.source: https://gltugs.wordpress.com/leo-a-mcarthur/ — verified: 2009 Penglai Bohai Shipyard, China; 5,384 bhp; 122ft; mated to heated asphalt barge John J. Carrick. CAVEAT: renamed Leo A. McArthur in 2017, so the AIS name is likely a stale static entry on the same hull — the fact remains true of that hull.
facts: China-built 2009 ATB tug — 5,384 hp pushing heated asphalt
She locks onto her barge using an Articouple articulated coupling system.
Her twin MaK diesel engines push the loaded barge at up to twelve knots.

vessels.name: JOHN J CARRICK
vessels.fact: Chinese-built heated asphalt barge — hauls 70,000 barrels
vessels.source: https://professionalmariner.com/another-new-atb-for-great-lakes-service-tug-victorious-is-second-unit-for-mcasphalt/ — BUILD YEAR CORRECTED 2008 -> 2009 (Penglai Bohai Shipyard). Length filled in at ~410ft LOA. 70,000 bbl and heated asphalt (to 350F) confirmed.
facts: Chinese-built heated asphalt barge — hauls 70,000 barrels
Her asphalt cargo rides near 350 degrees, kept molten by two one-million-BTU heaters.
She was given a ship-shaped bow, unusual for a barge, to shed winter ice.
She can pump her cargo ashore at up to 6,000 barrels an hour.

vessels.name: MENOMINEE
vessels.fact: Built 1952, stretched 72 ft in 1958, cut down to a barge in 2006
vessels.source: https://greatlakesships.wordpress.com/sparrows-point/ — ex-Sparrows Point. Lengthened 72ft at American Shipbuilding South Chicago over winter 1957-58; barged at Erie Marine 2006. LENGTH CORRECTED 698 -> 616ft (barge alone); 728ft only when combined with tug Olive L. Moore.
facts: Built 1952, stretched 72 ft in 1958, cut down to a barge in 2006
She began life as the Maryland-built iron-ore carrier Sparrows Point.
Across her long career she has carried four names, most recently Menominee.
She was rebuilt as a self-unloader in 1979 at Fraser Shipyards in Superior, Wisconsin.
Today the tug Olive L. Moore pushes her in the Great Lakes stone trade.

vessels.name: UNDAUNTED
vessels.fact: WWII Navy tug, then Kings Point training ship, now a barge pusher
vessels.source: https://gltugs.wordpress.com/undaunted/ — BUILD YEAR CORRECTED 1944 -> 1943 (ATA-199, Gulfport Boiler & Welding Works, Port Arthur TX). Decommissioned 1948; to Kings Point 1963 as Kings Pointer; now paired with barge Pere Marquette 41. Year is single-source; Wikipedia ATA-199 page not independently re-checked.
facts: WWII Navy tug, then Kings Point training ship, now a barge pusher
In 1945 she towed the crippled destroyer USS Hugh W. Hadley nearly 7,000 miles home.
She was built in Port Arthur, Texas, by Gulfport Boiler and Welding Works.
During the war she hauled floating dry-dock sections through the Panama Canal to Pacific bases.
In 1998 Basic Marine widened her and rebuilt her into an articulated barge tug.

vessels.name: PERE MARQUETTE 41
vessels.fact: Carried a million railcars in 47 years as a carferry
vessels.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_City_of_Midland_41 — the million-railcars/47-years claim CHECKS OUT (carferry 1941-1988, ~1 million cars, 3.5 million miles). LENGTH CORRECTED 403 -> 406ft. Launched Sept 1940, completed March 1941; barged 1997.
facts: Carried a million railcars in 47 years as a carferry
She entered service in 1941 as the carferry City of Midland 41, built by Manitowoc Shipbuilding.
When new she was the largest car ferry on the Great Lakes, nicknamed Queen of the Lakes.
She was driven by rare Skinner Unaflow steam engines.
Converted to a barge in 1997, she is now pushed by the tug Undaunted.

vessels.name: G L OSTRANDER
vessels.fact: Built 1976 in Louisiana as the Andrew Martin — renamed 2004
vessels.source: https://gltugs.wordpress.com/g-l-ostrander/ — built 1976 by Halter Marine, Pierre Part LA; ex-Andrew Martin; renamed 2004; pushes cement barge Integrity. REMOVED 'named for a Lafarge executive' — the source does NOT state the namesake, so that was unverified. Length 140ft 02in.
facts: Built 1976 in Louisiana as the Andrew Martin — renamed 2004
Before her current name she also sailed as Robert L. Torres and Jacklyn M.
She has been repowered twice and now makes 7,200 horsepower.
She pushes the cement barge Integrity as an articulated tug, managed by Andrie Incorporated.

vessels.name: INTEGRITY
vessels.fact: Cement barge built 1996 — 17,557 tons across eight holds
vessels.source: https://greatlakesships.wordpress.com/integrity/ — every element confirmed exactly: 1996, 460ft barge alone (544ft with tug), 17,557 tons, 8 holds, self-unloading cement carrier. No changes needed.
facts: Cement barge built 1996 — 17,557 tons across eight holds
She was built by Bay Shipbuilding in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin.
She unloads her cement through a Fuller-Kinyon pneumatic pump system.
Coupled to the tug G.L. Ostrander, the tandem stretches about 544 feet.

vessels.name: JOYCE L VANENKEVORT
vessels.fact: Just 135 ft of tug — pushes the 740-ft barge Great Lakes Trader
vessels.source: VERIFIED. gltugs.wordpress.com/joyce-l-vanenkevort/ gives LOA 135'04", built 1998 by Bay Shipbuilding; Great Lakes Trader barge confirmed at 740 ft LOA (vtbarge.com/vtbourfleet, greatlakesships.wordpress.com/great-lakes-trader/).
facts: Just 135 ft of tug — pushes the 740-ft barge Great Lakes Trader
Bay Shipbuilding in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin built her in 1998.
Twin Caterpillar diesels give her about 10,200 horsepower, among the most powerful tugs on the Lakes.
In May 2000 she sailed out the Seaway and down the Atlantic coast to New Orleans to fetch her barge.
Before her own barge arrived, she spent 1998 pushing Interlake's converted barge Pathfinder.

vessels.name: GREAT REPUBLIC
vessels.fact: Twin props and eight rudders — built to twist up the Cuyahoga
vessels.source: CORRECTED — original said 'four rudders'; boatnerd.com/vessel-info/great-lakes-fleet/great-republic/ documents an EIGHT-rudder system (two aft plus two flanking rudders per Kort-nozzled propeller). Length 634'10", launched 1981 at Bay Shipbuilding, purpose-built for the Cuyahoga River.
facts: Twin props and eight rudders — built to twist up the Cuyahoga
She was launched in 1981 as the American Republic and renamed Great Republic in 2011.
Her variable-pitch propellers spin inside strengthened Kort nozzles for extra thrust in tight rivers.
She's considered the most nimble and maneuverable ship in the world.
In the summer of 1996 she carried the Olympic flame on her deck in a lit cauldron at Cleveland.

vessels.name: KEN BOOTHE SR
vessels.fact: 135-ft, 10,700-hp tug built at Erie, PA to push a 740-ft barge
vessels.source: CORRECTED — the original superlative was mis-attributed: erieshipnews.blogspot.com applies 'first new bulk cargo vessel built in Erie in almost forty years' to the BARGE Lakes Contender, not to this tug. Replaced with tug specs verified in the same article (135 ft, 10,700 hp, Donjon Shipbuilding, Erie PA; christened 4/10/2012, so built year set to 2012 not 2011). CAUTION: this hull was reportedly renamed CLYDE S. VANENKEVORT after the VanEnkevort acquisition, so an AIS contact under the old name may be stale or a different vessel.
facts: 135-ft, 10,700-hp tug built at Erie, PA to push a 740-ft barge
Her construction stalled in the 2009 recession and was finished after Donjon took over the yard.
She was the second big articulated tug of her design, following the 1998 Joyce L. VanEnkevort.
Hydraulically operated toothed pins on her sides lock her into the barge's notch.
In 2017 VanEnkevort bought her and renamed her the Clyde S. VanEnkevort.

vessels.name: LAKES CONTENDER
vessels.fact: 740-ft self-unloading barge with no engines of its own
vessels.source: CORRECTED — dropped the disputed tonnage: erieshipnews.blogspot.com says 34,000 tons while greatlakesships.wordpress.com/lakes-contender/ says 38,516 tons, so no figure is safe to broadcast. The 740-ft length, 2012 build at Donjon Shipbuilding (Erie, PA) and the engineless articulated-barge design (Hydraconn ATB connection, pushed by a tug) are confirmed by both sources.
facts: 740-ft self-unloading barge with no engines of its own
Donjon built her at Erie, Pennsylvania, and christened her Lakes Contender in April 2012.
She can haul more than 38,000 tons of ore, coal, or stone.
Her cargo rides ashore on a 265-foot aft-mounted unloading boom.
In 2017 she was renamed Erie Trader after VanEnkevort bought her.

vessels.name: MARK W BARKER
vessels.fact: First new U.S.-built Great Lakes freighter since 1983
vessels.source: Interlake Steamship / Wikipedia / Professional Mariner
facts: First new U.S.-built Great Lakes freighter since 1983
She's named after Interlake Steamship's own president, Mark W. Barker.
She's the first ship on the Great Lakes powered by cleaner EPA Tier 4 engines.
Her unloading boom was salvaged from the scrapped steamer American Victory.
She's built to carry unusual cargo like wind-turbine blades on deck.

vessels.name: FEDERAL HAMILTON
vessels.fact: Fednav ocean-going saltie, ~656 ft, built 2023, Marshall Islands flag
vessels.source: vesselfinder.com IMO 9975363 (bulk carrier, 2023, 200 m, Marshall Islands); builder China per MarineLink (unconfirmed)
facts: One of Fednav's newest ocean-going bulk carriers, flagged in the Marshall Islands.
A Seaway-sized saltie about 656 feet long, built to transit the St. Lawrence Seaway locks into the Great Lakes.
Operated by Montreal-based Fednav, Canada's largest ocean-going dry-bulk shipowner.

vessels.name: FEDERAL CLYDE
vessels.fact: Fednav handysize laker, ~656 ft, built 2016 in Japan (Oshima)
vessels.source: vesselfinder/shipindex IMO 9671072 (bulk, 2016, Marshall Islands, 34,564 DWT); near-sister to Federal Cedar
facts: Built in 2016 as part of Fednav's box-hold handysize series of about 34,500 tons (Oshima Shipbuilding, Japan).
A Seaway-sized saltie roughly 656 feet long under the Marshall Islands flag.
A near-sister of the Federal Cedar, from the same 2016 Japanese-built class.

vessels.name: FEDERAL CEDAR
vessels.fact: Fednav saltie, ~656 ft, built 2016 by Oshima, Japan; runs FALLine
vessels.source: wikipedia/vesselfinder IMO 9671101 (bulk, 2016 Oshima Japan, 200 m, 34,564 DWT, Marshall Islands)
facts: Built in 2016 by Oshima Shipbuilding in Japan; a box-hold handysize bulker of about 34,500 tons.
A roughly 656-foot Seaway-sized saltie flagged in the Marshall Islands.
Sails Fednav's FALLine (Fednav Atlantic Lakes Line), a scheduled service linking Europe with the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence system.

vessels.name: FEDERAL HUNTER
vessels.fact: Fednav saltie, ~656 ft, built 2001 in Japan; Marshall Islands flag
vessels.source: vesselfinder IMO 9205938 (bulk, 2001, 200 m, Marshall Islands, 36,563 DWT); name collides with older unrelated ships
facts: Built in 2001 by Oshima Shipbuilding, Japan; a seaway-sized bulker of about 36,500 tons.
Roughly 656 feet long, now Marshall Islands flagged after earlier registration in Hong Kong.
One of the older salties still trading to the Great Lakes within the Fednav fleet.

vessels.name: FEDERAL YUKINA
vessels.fact: Fednav saltie, ~656 ft, built 2010; ~12% more fuel-efficient class
vessels.source: vesselfinder IMO 9476977 (bulk, 2010 Japan, 200 m, 35,868 DWT); Fednav/insidelogistics.ca on 2011 Hamilton call
facts: Built in 2010 in Japan; a seaway-sized saltie of about 35,900 tons, now Marshall Islands flagged.
When delivered, Fednav said she was about 12% more fuel-efficient than the previous class - roughly 770 tonnes of fuel saved a year.
On an early Lakes voyage in 2011 she carried industrial slag from Japan to Fednav's Hamilton, Ontario terminal.

vessels.name: FEDERAL WILLIAM PAUL
vessels.fact: Fednav's newest saltie, ~656 ft, built 2025; Marshall Islands flag
vessels.source: vesselfinder IMO 9975454 (bulk, 2025, 200 m, Marshall Islands); same 9975-series as Federal Hamilton
facts: One of Fednav's very newest bulk carriers, built in 2025 and flagged in the Marshall Islands.
A Seaway-sized saltie about 656 feet long, from the same recent series as the Federal Hamilton and Federal Minnesota.
Unusually for the 'Federal' fleet - most named for places or rivers - she carries a personal name.

vessels.name: POLSTEAM PILE
vessels.fact: Polsteam lakermax, ~656 ft, built 2024 in China; Portugal flag
vessels.source: gard.no/ajot.com IMO 9971886 (bulk, 2024 Shanhaiguan China, 200 m, 37,654 DWT, Portugal); 4th of 12 new Polsteam lakermaxes
facts: Built in 2024 at China's Shanhaiguan shipyard; the fourth of twelve new ~37,000-ton 'lakermax' bulkers ordered by Polsteam.
About 656 feet long, Portugal-flagged, and purpose-built to pass the locks into the Great Lakes.
In spring 2025 she was the first ocean vessel of the season at Burns Harbor, Indiana, delivering specialty steel. She is named for a Polish lake, Jezioro Pile.

vessels.name: POLSTEAM DABIE
vessels.fact: Polsteam lakermax, ~656 ft, built 2024; lead ship of a class of 12
vessels.source: gard.no/polsteam.com IMO 9971850 (bulk, 2024 Shanhaiguan China, 200 m, 37,591 DWT, Portugal); lead ship of 12. Pron: DOMB-yeh
facts: The lead ship - first of twelve - in Polsteam's new ~37,000-ton 'lakermax' series, built in 2024 in China.
About 656 feet long and Portugal-flagged; she reached the Great Lakes in April 2024.
Named for Lake Dabie near Polsteam's home port of Szczecin, Poland.

vessels.name: DRAWSKO
vessels.fact: Polsteam laker, ~623 ft, built 2010 in China; named for a Polish lake
vessels.source: vesselfinder/gard.no IMO 9393450 (bulk, 2010 Nantong China, 190 m, 30,000 DWT, Malta). Pron: DRAHV-skoh
facts: Built in 2010 in China; one of a series of ~30,000-ton lakers that Polsteam named after Polish lakes.
About 623 feet long, Malta-flagged, and sized to fit the St. Lawrence Seaway locks.
Named after Lake Drawsko in northwestern Poland.

vessels.name: BBC PHILIPPINES
vessels.fact: BBC Chartering F500 heavy-lift ship, two 250-ton cranes, ~482 ft (2023)
vessels.source: heavyliftpfi/Gard IMO 9963401 (2023 Taizhou SanFu China, 147 m, ~12,400 DWT, 2x250t cranes, F500 type)
facts: One of BBC Chartering's new F500-class heavy-lift vessels, built 2023 in China.
She carries two 250-tonne cranes - 500 tons combined - for project and heavy-lift cargo like wind-turbine and industrial parts.
German-managed by the Briese group of Leer and flagged in Antigua & Barbuda; about 482 feet long.

vessels.name: BBC EAGLE
vessels.fact: Multipurpose cargo ship sailing for BBC Chartering, ~456 ft (2008)
vessels.source: Gard/Marinelink IMO 9407574 (2008, 139 m, A&B); owned/managed by Juengerhans (ex 'Apus J'), BBC = charterer
facts: A multipurpose general-cargo ship built in 2008, trading for BBC Chartering under the Antigua & Barbuda flag.
Owned and managed by Germany's Juengerhans Maritime Services; she originally sailed as the Apus J.
About 456 feet long, carrying general and project cargo.

vessels.name: BBC VERMONT
vessels.fact: Multipurpose project-cargo ship for BBC Chartering, ~454 ft (2008)
vessels.source: Shipfix/WK Webster IMO 9357236 (2008, 138.5 m, A&B, ~12,800 DWT, up to 665 TEU)
facts: A multipurpose general-cargo ship built in 2008, flagged in Antigua & Barbuda.
She can carry up to about 665 containers plus general and project cargo - roughly 12,800 tons deadweight.
About 454 feet long, trading for BBC Chartering.

vessels.name: BBC ROSTOV
vessels.fact: BBC Chartering F500 heavy-lift ship, two 250-ton cranes, ~482 ft (2024)
vessels.source: Shipfix/heavyliftpfi IMO 9964443 (delivered ~2024, 147 m, A&B, ~12,400 DWT, F500 type)
facts: One of BBC Chartering's newest F500-class heavy-lift vessels, delivered around 2024.
She carries two 250-tonne cranes - 500 tons combined - for project and heavy-lift cargo.
German-managed by the Briese group of Leer and flagged in Antigua & Barbuda; about 482 feet long.

vessels.name: FLEVOBORG
vessels.fact: Royal Wagenborg ice-class multipurpose ship, built 2010 (Ferus Smit)
vessels.source: wagenborg.com/wikipedia IMO 9419292 (2010 Ferus Smit, ~14,600 DWT, Ice 1A, Delfzijl). LOA disputed (Wagenborg 154.6m vs aggregators ~142.8m) so length left off
facts: A Dutch multipurpose dry-cargo carrier built in 2010 by Ferus Smit; part of Royal Wagenborg's F-class.
Ice-class 1A and about 14,600 tons deadweight, with two box-shaped holds for general and project cargo; registered in Delfzijl.
Her name follows Wagenborg's convention of Dutch place names - here Flevoland, the reclaimed-land province.

vessels.name: FINNBORG
vessels.fact: Royal Wagenborg ice-class multipurpose ship, built 2011 (Ferus Smit)
vessels.source: wagenborg.com IMO 9419321 (2011 Ferus Smit, ~14,600 DWT, Ice 1A, Delfzijl); sister to Flevoborg/Fivelborg. LOA disputed, length left off
facts: A Royal Wagenborg F-class multipurpose dry-cargo ship, built in 2011 by Ferus Smit; sister to the Flevoborg and Fivelborg.
Ice-class 1A and about 14,600 tons deadweight; Dutch-flagged and registered in Delfzijl.
Two large open-hatch holds let her carry general and project cargo into the Great Lakes.

vessels.name: ELBEBORG
vessels.fact: Royal Wagenborg multipurpose cargo ship, ~474 ft (2011)
vessels.source: offshore-energy/Marinelink IMO 9568249 (2011 Royal Niestern Sander, ~144.6 m, ~12,000 DWT, Delfzijl)
facts: A Dutch multipurpose cargo ship built in 2011 by Royal Niestern Sander for Royal Wagenborg.
About 474 feet long and roughly 12,000 tons deadweight; registered in Delfzijl.
Her name echoes Wagenborg's river-name convention - the Elbe, a major European river.

vessels.name: FIVELBORG
vessels.fact: Royal Wagenborg ice-class multipurpose ship, built 2010 (Ferus Smit)
vessels.source: vesselfinder/wagenborg.com IMO 9419307 (2010 Ferus Smit, ~14,575 DWT, Ice 1A, Delfzijl); sister to Flevoborg/Finnborg. LOA disputed, length left off
facts: A Royal Wagenborg F-class multipurpose dry-cargo ship, built in 2010; sister to the Flevoborg and Finnborg.
Ice-class 1A and about 14,600 tons deadweight; Dutch-flagged with her home port in Delfzijl.
Her name recalls the Fivel, a historic river in the Groningen region of the Netherlands.

vessels.name: VLIEBORG
vessels.fact: Royal Wagenborg general-cargo ship, ~468 ft (2012)
vessels.source: scheepvaartwest/offshore-energy IMO 9554781 (2012 Ferus Smit Westerbroek, 142.65 m, Netherlands, Delfzijl)
facts: A Dutch general-cargo and multipurpose ship built in 2012 by Ferus Smit for Royal Wagenborg.
About 468 feet long and registered in Delfzijl.
Named after the Vlie, the tidal channel in the Wadden Sea between the islands of Vlieland and Terschelling.

vessels.name: HUMBERGRACHT
vessels.fact: Spliethoff heavy-lift ship, 300-ton cranes, ~454 ft (ex-BBC Montana)
vessels.source: MaritimeOptima/heavyliftpfi IMO 9433274 (2008-09 Taizhou Sanfu China, 138.5 m, ~12,770 DWT, 300t crane); ex HHL Tyne, orig. BBC Montana
facts: A Spliethoff heavy-lift and project-cargo ship with a combined crane capacity of 300 tonnes.
Built in China around 2008-09; she first sailed as the BBC Montana, then HHL Tyne, before Spliethoff bought her in 2019 and reflagged her Dutch.
About 454 feet long; the '-gracht' ending shared across Spliethoff's fleet is Dutch for 'canal'.

vessels.name: MACKINAW
vessels.fact: U.S. Coast Guard heavy icebreaker (WLBB-30), the Lakes' primary ice ship
vessels.source: wikipedia/USCG - USCGC Mackinaw WLBB-30, commissioned 2006, Marinette Marine WI, homeport Cheboygan MI
facts: The modern USCGC Mackinaw (WLBB-30), commissioned in 2006 and homeported in Cheboygan, Michigan, is the Great Lakes' primary heavy icebreaker.
Built by Marinette Marine in Wisconsin, she can break roughly 42 inches of level ice and also sets and tends navigation buoys.
She replaced the famous 1944 Mackinaw - now a museum ship in Mackinaw City - which was retired the same day in 2006.

vessels.name: CLYDE W. FOGG
vessels.fact: 1944 single-screw tug hauling freight to Beaver Island, Lake Michigan
vessels.source: gltugs.wordpress.com - built 1944 as US Army ST-709, renamed Clyde W. Fogg 2022 by St. James Marine of Charlevoix MI, registered Beaver Island | 2026-11 additions: gltugs.wordpress.com/susan-l-2 - Equitable Equipment New Orleans 1944, ST-709, Stanley 1947, Susan L 1999 Selvick Marine Towing, Clyde W. Fogg 2022, 86 ft, 700 bhp. gltugs.wordpress.com/st-james-marine-company - freight to the island from Ironton by tug and barge. tugboatinformation.com/company.cfm?id=2367 - Fogg Marine founded early 1970s by Clyde Fogg. ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/368268160 - Beaver Island port calls 2026 (lists 98 ft, conflicts with 86 ft).
facts: Built in 1944 as the U.S. Army tug ST-709; she served the Army Corps of Engineers for decades before civilian work.
Renamed Clyde W. Fogg in 2022 by St. James Marine of Charlevoix, Michigan; registered at Beaver Island, she mainly runs freight out to the island.
Equitable Equipment of New Orleans built her in 1944, and she has now had four names.
From 1947 to 1999 she was the Stanley, working on the Great Lakes for the Army Corps of Engineers.
Selvick Marine Towing of Sturgeon Bay bought her in 1999 and named her Susan L.
Her owners, Fogg Marine, began in the early 1970s when a man named Clyde Fogg started the business.
With a barge in tow she brings freight from Ironton, Michigan, out to the people of Beaver Island.

vessels.name: PRENTISS BROWN
vessels.fact: Cement tug pushing St. Marys barge St. Marys Conquest out of Charlevoix
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com/WMHS - built 1967 TX (ex Betty Culbreath), Port City Marine 2008, deep-notch rebuild 2009; pushes barge St. Marys Conquest
facts: Built in 1967 in Texas, she was rebuilt in 2009 for deep-notch pushing and renamed Prentiss Brown.
At 4,300 horsepower she pushes the cement barge St. Marys Conquest for St. Marys Cement, loading at Charlevoix, Michigan.
She is almost certainly named for Prentiss M. Brown, the St. Ignace senator known as the 'father of the Mackinac Bridge.'

vessels.name: DONALD J SARTER
vessels.fact: Great Lakes Towing harbor & ship-assist tug, 3,000 hp, built 1964
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com/Great Lakes Group - built 1964 Main Iron Works LA (ex Point Comfort), renamed 2020, acquired by Great Lakes Towing 2022
facts: Built in 1964 in Louisiana as the Point Comfort, she was renamed Donald J. Sarter by Sarter Marine in 2020.
The Great Lakes Towing Company of Cleveland took her over in 2022; she does harbor towing and ship assist across the Lakes.
A twin-screw tug rated at about 3,000 horsepower.

vessels.name: CANDACE ELISE
vessels.fact: Ashton Marine tug on the tank barge Robert F. Deegan - calcium chloride
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com/Mason County Press - built 1981 LA (ex Perseverance), Ashton Marine of North Muskegon MI 2015; pairs with barge Robert F. Deegan
facts: Built in 1981 in Louisiana, she was acquired and renamed Candace Elise by Ashton Marine of North Muskegon, Michigan in 2015.
She pairs with the 225-foot tank barge Robert F. Deegan, hauling liquid calcium chloride for OxyChem's Ludington, Michigan plant.
Powered by twin Caterpillar diesels at about 2,600 horsepower.

vessels.name: MEREDITH ASHTON
vessels.fact: Ashton Marine's 4,000-hp tug, also runs the tank barge Robert F. Deegan
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com/Mason County Press - built 1999 Thoma-Sea LA (ex Nutmeg State), Ashton Marine of North Muskegon MI; sister to Candace Elise
facts: Built in 1999 in Louisiana, she is Ashton Marine's larger tug at about 4,000 horsepower.
She also works the tank barge Robert F. Deegan serving the OxyChem plant at Ludington, Michigan.
A twin-screw tug and sister vessel to the Candace Elise, out of North Muskegon, Michigan.

vessels.name: KRISTIN JOELLE
vessels.fact: Ryba Marine construction & towing tug out of Cheboygan, MI (built 1965)
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com - built 1965 Equitable Equipment LA (ex Vincent J. Robin IV), renamed by Ryba Marine 2017, homeport Cheboygan MI
facts: Built in 1965 in Louisiana, she carried many names before Ryba Marine renamed her Kristin Joelle in 2017.
Owned by Ryba Marine Construction and homeported in Cheboygan, Michigan - the same port as the icebreaker Mackinaw.
Repowered with twin Caterpillar diesels at about 2,400 horsepower.

vessels.name: MATT ALLEN
vessels.fact: 1961 Great Lakes tug of the King Co. of Holland, MI (ex-Mari Beth Andrie)
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com (USCG Doc 287250) - built 1961 Golden Meadow LA (ex Gladys Bea), King Co./RDK LLC of Holland MI, ex-Mari Beth Andrie | 2026-11 additions: gltugs.wordpress.com/matt-allen - came to the Great Lakes 1973, active for King Company in dredge and construction trades on Lake Michigan, 80 ft 4 in, 2,200 bhp, two Detroit 12V-149. tugboatinformation.com/tug.cfm?id=3212 - name and owner chain, Tidewater Dredge of Chicago, Bultema of Muskegon, Canonie, Andrie, King Co., RDK LLC.
facts: Built in 1961 in Louisiana as the Gladys Bea, she is an 80-foot, 2,200-horsepower twin-screw tug.
Owned by the King Company of Holland, Michigan; she earlier worked for Andrie Inc. of Muskegon as the Mari Beth Andrie.
She has sailed under four names: Gladys Bea, American Viking, Mari Beth Andrie and now Matt Allen.
She reached the Great Lakes in 1973, when Tidewater Dredge and Construction of Chicago named her American Viking.
Two Detroit Diesel engines give her 2,200 horsepower and turn twin propellers.
She stays busy on dredging and construction jobs around Lake Michigan.

vessels.name: KIMBERLY JOY
vessels.fact: Ryba Marine's Cheboygan tug - built 1942 as Coast Guard cutter Manitou
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com - built 1942 as USCGC Manitou (WYT-60), civilian 1984, acquired 2024 by Ryba Marine Construction of Cheboygan MI | 2026-11 additions: gltugs.wordpress.com/manitou - Coast Guard Yard Baltimore, Malcolm Marine 1984-2024, rebuilt from the deck up, back in service 1996, dredging, construction, icebreaking and ship assist (lists 110 ft). tugboatinformation.com/tug.cfm?id=13821 - decommissioned Nov 1980, repowered 1996 with EMD 16-645, Ryba 2024, 104.9 ft, 2,200 hp.
facts: Built in 1942 as the U.S. Coast Guard cutter Manitou, she was sold into civilian work in 1984.
A 105-foot, 2,200-horsepower tug acquired in 2024 by Ryba Marine Construction of Cheboygan - right at the Straits.
She was built at the Coast Guard's own shipyard in Baltimore and served as an icebreaking tug until 1980.
Malcolm Marine of St. Clair, Michigan, bought her in 1984 and kept the name Manitou for the next 40 years.
Malcolm rebuilt her from the deck up over more than a decade, and she returned to work in 1996.
Today she helps with dredging and construction jobs, and she can still break ice and assist ships in port.

vessels.name: VOLGABORG
vessels.fact: Dutch Wagenborg saltie with a bulb-free bow that slices through waves.
vessels.source: IMO 9631072. ferussmit.com launch notice: size, bulbless bow, ice-friendly stem, Winschoterdiep record. shiphotos.com ID 572: IMO, 2013 launch, length, Wagenborg manager, Delfzijl registry. importinfo.com: Great Lakes port calls and 2026 cargoes. wagenborg.com: river-plus-borg naming. Wikipedia Volga: longest river in Europe.
facts: She is managed by Wagenborg of Delfzijl in the Netherlands and measures 468 feet, with room for about 12,000 tons.
Her builders gave her a bulbless bow, whose long sharp lines ease her through the water and help her cut through rough seas.
The shape of her bow also helps her push through sheets of ice.
In August 2026 she brought paperboard from Kemi, Finland, to Green Bay, after carrying ferrochrome from Finland to Toledo that April.
Wagenborg likes to name ships for rivers and add the ending borg, and the Volga is the longest river in Europe.

vessels.name: FULDABORG
vessels.fact: River-style Wagenborg name, ice-class hull, and a Chicago regular.
vessels.source: IMO 9559092. Wagenborg F-class data sheet (wagenborg.com PDF): sister list, Ferus Smit yard, ice class, Lakes fitted, 154.6 m length, holds, movable bulkheads. vesselfinder, magicport: 2012 build, Dutch flag. importinfo.com: 71 US port calls, Green Bay Oct 2026. wagenborg.com: naming custom. Wikipedia Fulda river.
facts: She is one of six Wagenborg F-class sisters built by Ferus Smit, all with Finnish and Swedish 1A ice class and fitted for the Great Lakes.
Her two box-shaped holds offer more than 600,000 cubic feet of space, and movable bulkheads let the crew reshape them to suit a cargo.
U.S. records list 71 port calls for her, led by Chicago, Cleveland and Detroit.
In October 2026 she called at Green Bay with about 8,000 tons of cargo.
Her name follows the Wagenborg river custom, and the Fulda is a German river of about 137 miles.

vessels.name: FRASERBORG
vessels.fact: Wagenborg F-class saltie that carries Swedish steel to Chicago.
vessels.source: IMO 9419319. Wagenborg F-class data sheet (wagenborg.com PDF): sister list, ice class, Lakes fitted, 154.6 m length. vesselfinder, magicport: 2011 build, Dutch flag, Wagenborg manager. importinfo.com: 68 US port calls, Aug 2026 Chicago steel from Oxelosund. wagenborg.com: naming custom. Wikipedia Fraser River.
facts: In August 2026 she brought hot-rolled steel coils and plates from Oxelosund, Sweden, to Chicago.
U.S. records show 68 port calls for her since 2013, with Chicago, Detroit and Cleveland as her recent regulars.
She and Fuldaborg are sisters in the six-ship Wagenborg F-class, built for ice and fitted for the Great Lakes.
Her name follows the Wagenborg river custom, and the Fraser is the longest river wholly inside British Columbia.

vessels.name: EGBERT WAGENBORG
vessels.fact: Named for Wagenborg's founder, with her bridge up near the bow.
vessels.source: IMO 9802695. wagenborg.com EasyMax story: forward bridge, size, Seaway routes, largest built inland in the northern Netherlands. portnews.ru christening report: founder's name, third ship in 67 years, first voyage. portwindsor.com: first saltie of 2023, challenge coin. importinfo.com: Oct 2026 Chicago steel. vesselfinder: specs, flag.
facts: She honors Egbert Wagenborg, who founded the Dutch company in 1898, and by 2017 she was the third company ship in 67 years to carry his name.
Her bridge and cabins sit toward the bow, which frees up cargo space and gives clear views over her load.
On April 4, 2023 she became the first saltie of the season at Port Windsor and was welcomed with the port's challenge coin.
In October 2026 she brought hot-rolled steel coils from Oxelosund, Sweden, to Chicago.
When new she was the largest ship ever built in the northern Netherlands on the land side of the dikes.

vessels.name: HEEMSKERKGRACHT
vessels.fact: Dutch crane ship that brought 15 engine generators to Cleveland.
vessels.source: IMO 9443669. spliethoff.com H-type page: sister ships, cranes, Great Lakes fitted. Spliethoff 2025 fleet list: 138.07 m, 2 x 180 mt cranes. spliethoff.com about page: canal naming since 1946. breakbulk.news: ex HHL Nile, bought 2016. importinfo.com: Duluth, Chicago and Cleveland 2026 calls, Aug 2026 cargo. vesselfinder: specs, flag.
facts: Spliethoff of Amsterdam has named its ships for canals since 1946, and gracht is the Dutch word for canal.
Her two deck cranes lift 180 tons each and can team up for 360 tons.
In August 2026 she reached Cleveland with 15 Wartsila engine generators for a power plant, plus a motor yacht on its own cradle.
She started out as HHL Nile, and Spliethoff bought and renamed her in 2016.
She reached Duluth twice in 2026, in June and August, which took her all the way up Lake Superior.

vessels.name: POLSTEAM OKRA
vessels.fact: New Polish laker-max named for a small lake in West Pomerania.
vessels.source: IMO 9984819. marinepoland.com: lake name, handover, fifth of 12, size. dailymare.com: maiden voyage, Madeira flag. shiphotos.com ID 68706: 200 m, Polsteam manager. importinfo.com: 2026 Great Lakes calls, Dutch steel to Chicago.
facts: Polsteam names its lake-class ships for Polish lakes, and Okra is a small lake in the Drawskie Lake District.
She is the fifth of twelve laker-max ships, handed over at the Shanhaiguan yard in China in January 2025.
Her maiden voyage took steel from China across the Pacific and through the Panama Canal to Cleveland and Milwaukee.
At 656 feet she is nearly two football fields long, sized to fit the locks on the way to the Great Lakes.
In August 2026 she brought steel from IJmuiden in the Netherlands to Chicago.

vessels.name: POLSTEAM LEBSKO
vessels.fact: Laker-max named for a shallow lake in a Polish national park.
vessels.source: IMO 9971874. polandatsea.com launch report: lake name, third of 12, Welland Canal design. Wikipedia Lebsko Lake: area, depth. vesselfinder: 199.99 m, 2024, Portugal (Madeira) flag. importinfo.com: Chicago, Milwaukee and Cleveland calls, 2026 Dutch steel cargoes.
facts: She is named for Lake Lebsko, near the town of Leba in Slowinski National Park on Poland's Baltic coast.
Her namesake lake covers about 28 square miles yet averages only about 5 feet deep.
She is the third of twelve sisters, designed to fit the eight locks of the Welland Canal, which lift ships about 330 feet.
In April 2026 she brought coiled tinplate and other steel from IJmuiden in the Netherlands to Milwaukee and Chicago.

vessels.name: POLSTEAM KOPROWO
vessels.fact: Second of Polsteam's 12 laker-maxes, named for a Wolin Island lake.
vessels.source: IMO 9971862. polandatsea.com: lake name, second of 12, yard, maiden voyage. vesselfinder: 199.99 m, 2024, Portugal (Madeira) flag; some trackers still show Liberia. importinfo.com: Milwaukee Dec 2024 tinplate, Chicago, Toledo Aug 2026.
facts: She takes her name from a lake on Wolin Island in Poland, and she is a lake ship in both senses.
She is the second of twelve laker-max bulk carriers built at the Shanhaiguan yard in Qinhuangdao, China.
On her first voyage in April 2024 she carried steel from China and South Korea to Hamilton and Windsor by way of the Panama Canal.
In December 2024 she brought almost 10,000 tons of coiled tinplate from the Netherlands to Milwaukee.

vessels.name: POLSTEAM WADAG
vessels.fact: One of the newest salties here, with a methanol-ready design.
vessels.source: IMO 1027196. marinepoland.com: tenth of 12, methanol-ready, maiden voyage, size, Madeira flag. vesselfinder: 2026, Portugal flag, Calumet Nov 2026. olsztyn.eu and visit.olsztyn.eu: Lake Wadag location. marinepoland.com Okra article: Polish lake naming custom.
facts: She joined Polsteam in 2026 as the tenth of twelve laker-max ships.
Her design is ready to run on methanol as well as conventional fuel.
Her maiden voyage carried aluminium ingots from Port Klang, Malaysia, to Turkey and Bulgaria.
Polsteam names these ships for Polish lakes, and Lake Wadag lies east of the city of Olsztyn.

vessels.name: MAMRY
vessels.fact: Polsteam bulker sharing her name with Poland's second-largest lake.
vessels.source: IMO 9496264. shiphotos.com ID 8124: builder, launch, Polsteam manager. naviecapitani.it: 189.6 m, Bahamas flag, three cranes. Wikipedia Polsteam: 30,000-ton group. Wikipedia Lake Mamry: second largest, about 40 sq mi, 33 islands. importinfo.com: 28 US port calls, Aug 2026 Chicago coils from Turkey.
facts: She is managed by Polsteam, the Polish Steamship Company of Szczecin, and is one of eight 30,000-ton ships built in China.
She shares her name with Lake Mamry in Poland's Masurian Lake District, a lake of about 40 square miles with 33 islands.
She carries three cranes of her own for handling cargo.
In August 2026 she brought 162 coils of cold-rolled steel from Turkey to Chicago.

vessels.name: JUNO
vessels.fact: Polish-run saltie who shares her name with a Masurian lake.
vessels.source: IMO 9422378 (this is the Polsteam ship, not an older Great Lakes Juno). magicport, gard.no: 2011, 189 m, Bahamas flag, Polsteam manager. Wikipedia Polsteam: 30,000-ton group with Mamry. Duluth News Tribune: left Duluth Oct 8, 2024 for Bilbao. importinfo.com: 29 US port calls, 2026 Chicago steel from Turkey. komoot, slowhop: Lake Juno at Mragowo.
facts: She is managed by Polsteam, the Polish Steamship Company, and is a fleet sister of Mamry in the 30,000-ton group.
She shares her name with Lake Juno, which sits beside the town of Mragowo in Poland's Masurian region.
In October 2024 she left Duluth bound for Bilbao, Spain, a trip of about two and a half weeks.
In June 2026 she brought hot-rolled steel from Aliaga, Turkey, to Chicago.
U.S. records show 29 port calls for her, with Chicago the most frequent at 11.

vessels.name: SHIPKA
vessels.fact: Bulgarian bulker, the fourth ship in her fleet to carry the name.
vessels.source: IMO 9937282. hellenicshippingnews.com and navbul.com: fourth Shipka, Shipka Peak, sixth of 12, 1979 lake-fitted ship. maritimeoptima, magicport: 190 m, Malta flag. michiganexposures blog: seen on the Detroit River in 2024, fits Welland Canal. importinfo.com: Toledo and Buffalo 2026 cargoes.
facts: She belongs to Navigation Maritime Bulgare and is the fourth company ship named for Shipka Peak.
An earlier Shipka, from 1979, was the first Bulgarian bulk carrier fitted for lake service.
She is the sixth of twelve 32,150-ton sisters built at the Jiangsu Yangzi Xinfu yard in China.
In 2026 she brought rock salt from Alexandria, Egypt, to Toledo and raw cane sugar from Argentina to Buffalo.

vessels.name: BBC TORNIO
vessels.fact: New ice-strengthened heavy-lifter working for BBC Chartering.
vessels.source: IMO 1056276. heavyliftpfi.com July 2025: F500 delivery to Briese, ice class and winter ports. bbc-chartering.com company page: name meaning, F500 lifting, ice-class ships. vesselfinder: 147 m, 2025, flag, Burns Harbor Nov 2026. magicport: Briese manager. Wikipedia Tornio: town facts.
facts: The BBC in her name has nothing to do with television: it stands for Briese Bischoff Company, from Germany.
Her strengthened 1A ice class lets her work the northern Gulf of Bothnia and the St. Lawrence River in harsh winters.
She is an F500-type ship, a family built around cranes that can lift 500 tons together.
She shares her name with Tornio, a Finnish town on the border with Sweden.
In November 2026 she was reported leaving Burns Harbor, Indiana, on Lake Michigan.

vessels.name: BBC SEBASTOPOL
vessels.fact: Heavy-lifter whose two Liebherr cranes can lift 500 tons together.
vessels.source: IMO 9812004. bbc-chartering.com Nov 2022 news: builder, owner, size, cranes, engine, first voyage. vesselfinder: flag, 2022, Hamilton Nov 2026. importinfo.com: Chicago Oct 2026, 2026 cargoes.
facts: Her two Liebherr heavy-lift cranes can work as a team to lift up to 500 tons.
She was built by Taizhou Sanfu in China and joined the BBC Chartering fleet in October 2022.
She is owned and managed by Briese Schiffahrts of Leer, Germany, a sister company of BBC Chartering.
In 2026 her cargoes included about 6,900 tons of steel tubes from Turkey and compressor equipment from Japan.
In fall 2026 she called at Chicago in October and Hamilton, Ontario, in November.

vessels.name: BBC DUBAI
vessels.fact: LakerMax heavy-lifter built as big as Seaway locks and bridges allow.
vessels.source: IMO 9885312. bairdmaritime.com: builder, charter, triple-deck design, cranes, Seaway fit. shiphotos.com ID 68808: 149.95 m, flag, BBC fleet. bbc-chartering.com and maritimemag.com: 15 LakerMax ships, name meaning, forward bridge. importinfo.com: Duluth and Chicago Aug 2026, Linde project cargo from Mumbai.
facts: She is one of fifteen LakerMax ships, so named because their size is maxed out to still fit Seaway locks and bridges.
She is a triple-decker whose deck panels lock in at different heights to suit the cargo.
With her cranes on one side, she keeps about 2,830 square meters of open deck, more than half a football field.
In August 2026 she brought equipment from Mumbai, India, to Chicago and Duluth for a project in Alberta, Canada.
She was built by Taizhou Sanfu in China and works on long-term charter to BBC Chartering.

vessels.name: FEDERAL BRISTOL
vessels.fact: Fednav of Montreal's Seaway-sized bulker, a regular with European steel.
vessels.source: IMO 9697844. vesselfinder: 199.98 m, 2015, flag, Milwaukee Nov 2026. motorship.com: Oshima at Saiki, third-generation Lakes-dimensioned series, fuel saving. Wikipedia Fednav: founded 1944, Montreal. importinfo.com: 27 US port calls, Oct 2026 coils from Aviles.
facts: She sails for Fednav, a privately owned Canadian company based in Montreal and founded in 1944.
She was built by Oshima in Saiki, Japan, as part of a series sized for the Great Lakes.
Her class uses about 25 percent less fuel than similar ships built 15 to 20 years earlier.
In October 2026 she brought 374 coils of steel, roughly 3,500 tons, from Aviles, Spain, to Milwaukee.
U.S. records show 27 port calls for her since 2016, mostly at Chicago, Milwaukee and Cleveland.

vessels.name: INDUSTRIAL SKIPPER
vessels.fact: Heavy-lift ship with two 250-ton cranes, built for oversize cargo.
vessels.source: IMO 9741138. shippingtelegraph.com: F500 type, 2 x 250 t cranes, 147 m, Intermarine charter. naviecapitani.it: Shandong Huanghai yard, July 2016 delivery. vesselfinder: flag, 2016. importinfo.com: Chicago Aug 2026, 2023 Algoma and Konecranes cargoes.
facts: Her two cranes lift 250 tons each and can combine for 500 tons.
She was delivered in July 2016 from the Shandong Huanghai yard in Rongcheng, China.
Intermarine chartered her long term in 2024 as part of a group of four heavy-lift ships.
In August 2023 her cargo included 283 pieces of steelmaking furnace equipment for Algoma Steel, about 1,130 tons.
That same month she also carried steel crane structures from Croatia to Chicago.

vessels.name: HARVEST SPIRIT
vessels.fact: McKeil Marine's crane-equipped bulker, a grain hauler on the Thunder Bay run.
vessels.type: Canadian geared bulk carrier (Great Lakes and Seaway trader)
vessels.source: IMO 9655951. mckeil.com fleet page: 152.50 m, four holds, cargo types, 16,737 tonnes. portofmonroe.com March 2023: three cranes, McKeil purchase 2020, routes, Turkey build, former names. vesselfinder, magicport: Canadian flag, McKeil owner (the McKeil page still lists Malta). McKeil spec sheet: in business since 1956.
facts: She works for McKeil Marine, a Canadian company operating since 1956, which bought her in 2020.
She was built in Turkey in 2012 as Zealand Juliana and later sailed as Juliana.
She has four cargo holds and three deck cranes, which are handy for coiled steel.
Her regular route carries grain between Thunder Bay and Windsor, Ontario.
She has also run steel coils from Nanticoke, Ontario, to Monroe, Michigan.

vessels.name: VICTORY
vessels.fact: Tug that pushes the barge Maumee, stone, coal and ore from Superior to Erie
vessels.type: Articulated tug-barge unit (tug Victory with barge Maumee)
vessels.source: wmhs.org/?p=3506 - pairing with Maumee, 804-ft unit length, 25,500 tons, renamed Victory/Maumee 2019, barge built 1953 as Reserve. gltugs.wordpress.com/victory - trades, route, tallest-tug claim, 7,880 bhp. tugboatinformation.com/tug.cfm?id=894 - Texaco 1981 build, pilothouse raised 8 ft, Gulf and Bahamas work. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_L._Kuber_(lake_freighter) - barge history. 'built' is the tug's year; lengthFt is the combined unit.
facts: She works as a matched pair with the self-unloading barge Maumee, which sailed for years as the James L. Kuber.
Her barge started life in 1953 as the freighter Reserve, so the pair blends a 1981 tug with a much older hull.
Fastened together they stretch 804 feet, more than two football fields, and can carry about 25,500 tons.
Built for Texaco, she worked Gulf of Mexico and Bahamas ports before coming to the Great Lakes in 2006.
Her pilothouse was raised high for barge work, and one Great Lakes tug site calls her the tallest tug on the Lakes.

vessels.name: NORTHERN VENTURE
vessels.fact: McKeil Marine's first self-unloader, with a 260-foot unloading boom
vessels.source: masoncountypress.com (2025 Ludington debut, 2026 Manistee chase story) - built 1998 Shin Kurushima Japan as Asia Cement No. 7, later Da Shen, McKeil 2022, 508.5 ft, 260-ft boom, 50-degree holds, 40 gates, trap rock from Bruce Mines. marinelog.com/news/mckeil-marine-thordonizes-self-discharging-bulker - water-lubricated bearings, COSCO Nantong refit, 19,651 dwt. McKeil announcement via search - first self-unloader in its fleet.
facts: She was built in Japan in 1998 as Asia Cement No. 7, then worked Asian waters as Da Shen.
McKeil Marine of Burlington, Ontario, bought her in 2022 and refitted her in China as its first self-unloader.
Four holds sloped at 50 degrees let her cargo slide down to 40 hydraulic gates and onto conveyor belts below.
Her propeller shaft bearings run on water rather than oil, which helps keep grease out of the Great Lakes.
She hauls trap rock from Bruce Mines, Ontario, and has passed under two drawbridges to reach Manistee Lake.

vessels.name: REBECCA LYNN
vessels.fact: Andrie asphalt tug, a 1964 Texas-built saltwater veteran
vessels.source: gltugs.wordpress.com/rebecca-lynn - built 1964 Port Arthur TX as Katherine Clewis, 112 ft 7 in, 3,600 bhp, saltwater dry bulk barges, Andrie 1996, works with tank barge Endurance in asphalt trades. tugboatinformation.com/tug.cfm?id=5614 - owner Andrie, Norton Shores MI. mikeyuhas.org/albums/marine/20244906.php - photographed with Endurance at Milwaukee Sept 2024.
facts: She was built in Port Arthur, Texas, in 1964 and first sailed as the Katherine Clewis.
Her early years were spent in salt water, moving dry bulk barges for Gulfcoast Transit.
Andrie of Muskegon brought her to the Great Lakes in 1996 and gave her the name Rebecca Lynn.
These days she usually teams up with the tank barge Endurance to move asphalt, the stuff that paves our roads.
Two big EMD diesels give her 3,600 horsepower and turn twin propellers.

vessels.name: ALGOTITAN
vessels.fact: Algoma product tanker carrying refined fuels, formerly the Chantaco
vessels.source: seawayreview.com/algoma-central-corporation-acquires-two-product-tankers - ex Chantaco, built 2007, 18,894 dwt, Great Lakes and St. Lawrence service. marinelog.com/news/algoma-central-acquires-2007-built-products-tanker-pair - purchase of sister pair. magicport.ai/vessels/tanker/algotitan-mmsi-316050854 - IMO 9333802, 143 m LOA, 23.4 m beam, Canadian flag, Algoma Tankers, Canadian ports. shiphotos.com sister ship entry - 143.29 m (470.1 ft). en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algoma_Central - fleet list.
facts: She is a tanker, not a bulk carrier, and moves refined petroleum products around the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence.
Algoma Central bought her and her sister Algoberta in December 2022 to prepare for replacing two older ships.
She sailed as the Chantaco before joining the Canadian flag in January 2023.
She is about 470 feet long and rated at 18,894 deadweight tonnes.
Her recent stops include Montreal, Valleyfield, Port Colborne and Nanticoke.

vessels.name: CG KATMAI BAY
vessels.fact: Lead ship of the Coast Guard's 140-foot icebreaking tugs
vessels.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Katmai_Bay - 140 ft, Tacoma Boatbuilding, commissioned 8 Jan 1979, lead of class, name origin, Sault Ste. Marie, operates in support of Mackinaw. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay-class_tugboat - bubbling system, 20 in continuous, 3 ft by ramming. dcms.uscg.mil CG-9 and shephardmedia.com - service-life work 2018. 'built' is the commissioning year.
facts: She is the first of the Coast Guard's Bay-class icebreaking tugs, commissioned in January 1979.
Her name comes from a saltwater shoreline in Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska.
Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan, is her home, and she works alongside the much larger icebreaker Mackinaw.
Her class can keep moving through 20 inches of freshwater ice and can break three-foot ice by ramming it.
Air bubbled along her hull helps her slip through ice with less resistance.

vessels.name: CG NEAH BAY
vessels.fact: Cleveland-based Coast Guard icebreaking tug, 140 feet long
vessels.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Neah_Bay - name origin, Tacoma Boatbuilding, launched and commissioned 1980, Cleveland, bubbler system. atlanticarea.uscg.mil Neah Bay unit page via search - Great Lakes-wide service. marinelink.com/news/maritime/neah-bay - 20 in continuous, 3 ft ramming, Lake Erie ice work. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay-class_tugboat - nine in class.
facts: She is named for Neah Bay, an inlet in Washington state, though her home is Cleveland, Ohio.
She can push steadily through 20 inches of hard freshwater ice, then back up and ram through more than three feet.
A low-pressure bubbler forces air and water between her hull and the ice so she needs less power to get through.
She is one of nine Bay-class tugs, and she helps keep freighters moving when Lake Erie ices up.
Commissioned in 1980, she works across the entire Great Lakes system.

vessels.name: CGC SEQUOIA
vessels.fact: 225-foot Coast Guard buoy tender based in Port Huron, Michigan
vessels.type: US Coast Guard seagoing buoy tender
vessels.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USCGC_Sequoia - 225 ft, Marinette Marine, launched 2003, commissioned 2004, Guam then Port Huron, 16 Juniper class. wgrt.com/coast-guard-cutter-sequoia-arrives-in-port-huron - arrival 7 Sept 2024, 19-day trip, replaces Hollyhock. atlanticarea.uscg.mil Sequoia unit page via search (direct fetch blocked) - nearly 150 aids on the lower Great Lakes. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juniper-class_cutter - station keeping, tree names.
facts: She looks after nearly 150 buoys and other navigation aids on the lower Great Lakes.
Marinette Marine in Wisconsin built her, so her move to Port Huron in 2024 was a homecoming to the Lakes.
Before Michigan she spent years in Guam as the buoy tender for the Marianas, a long way from any lake.
Her class can hold its spot within a 10-metre circle using computers and thrusters while the crew sets a buoy.
She is one of 16 Juniper-class tenders, a family with many ships named for trees.

vessels.name: DAVID R. SCHANOCK
vessels.fact: Roen Salvage tug from Sturgeon Bay, once owned on Kauai, Hawaii
vessels.source: tugboatinformation.com/tug.cfm?id=13077 and gltugs.wordpress.com/david-r-schanock - 1978 Main Iron Works, Itco XVI, H.A. Walker of Lihue Plantation in Hawaii, Trevor of Weeks Marine 1994, Roen 2021, 69 ft, 1,500 hp, twin Caterpillar C32. vesselfinder.com IMO 7939638 - US tug, built 1978. aol.com Door County firm story - David Schanock president since 2022, company founded 1949, fourth generation, tug and scows bound for Sault Ste. Marie April 2024.
facts: She started out in 1978 in Louisiana as the Itco XVI and was sold to a Hawaiian plantation company that same year.
She kept the name H.A. Walker until Weeks Marine of New Jersey made her the Trevor in 1994.
Roen Salvage of Sturgeon Bay bought her in 2021, and she shares her name with company president David Schanock.
Roen is a fourth-generation family company founded in 1949 that builds docks and breakwaters and does dredging.
In April 2024 she headed out with two deck scows for a dredging job near Sault Ste. Marie.

vessels.name: WEST SHORE
vessels.fact: 1947 Mackinac Island ferry, back under her original name since 2025
vessels.type: Mackinac Island passenger and freight ferry
vessels.source: arnoldtransitcompany.com/?p=10318 (A Legacy on the Water: The Story of West Shore) - built 1947 Sturgeon Bay, 64 ft 10 in, Miller Boat Line, 12 vehicles and 235 passengers, Beaver Island freight, Anna May from 2013, name restored 2025, 150 passengers or 47,000 lb, oldest-ferry claim is the company's own.
facts: She was built in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin, in 1947 to carry cars and people on Lake Erie.
Her first owner, Miller Boat Line of Put-in-Bay, Ohio, could fit 12 vehicles and 235 passengers aboard.
A Beaver Island owner later used her to haul freight, and she then sailed as the Anna May, carrying food and supplies.
Arnold Transit brought back her original name and colors in 2025 and calls her the oldest ferry still serving Mackinac Island.
She can carry up to 150 passengers or 47,000 pounds of freight.

vessels.name: NEESKAY
vessels.fact: UW-Milwaukee research boat whose name means pure, clean water
vessels.source: milwaukeeindependent.com/articles/research-vessel-neeskay-a-vital-tool-for-great-lakes-study - built 1953 Higgins New Orleans, 71 ft, name meaning, UWM 1970. uwm.edu/freshwater fleet page - 71 ft, 750-mile range, only year-round research vessel on the Lakes. yahoo.com/news/uwms-neeskay... - algae, mussels, microbes, buoys. wpr.org/news/neeskay-boat-research-vessel-winter-great-lakes-uw-milwaukee - winter work, mid-lake reef. uwm.edu Maggi Sue pages - planned 120-ft successor.
facts: Her name comes from the Ho-Chunk language and means pure, clean water.
The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee bought her in 1970 and turned the 71-foot workboat into a floating science lab.
UWM calls her the only research vessel on the Great Lakes that works year-round.
Scientists aboard study algae blooms, invasive quagga and zebra mussels, and tiny microbes in the water.
She also sets and tends buoys that report weather, water temperature and nutrients from out on the lake.

vessels.name: LAKE ERIE
vessels.fact: 607-foot saltie with three deck cranes, formerly the Federal Matane
vessels.source: gard.no/vessels/43891 - Lake Erie, IMO 9283540, bulk carrier, Antigua and Barbuda, built 2004, ex Federal Matane. erieshipnews.blogspot.com (Federal Matane label) - 2004 Wenchong Shipyard, 607 ft, three 30-tonne cranes, 27,781 tonnes at 9.8 m, 20,100 at Seaway draft, Fednav. ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/304604000 - Port Weller 20 Oct 2026, Calumet Harbor 28 Oct 2026, Thunder Bay and Hamilton earlier in 2026. shipspotting.com/photos/3506545 via search - name chain Lake Erie, Federal Matane, CL Hanse Gate, Hanse Gate.
facts: She is an ocean-crossing freighter, known on the Lakes as a saltie, and she came through the Seaway in 2026.
China's Wenchong Shipyard built her in 2004, and at 607 feet she is about as long as two football fields.
Three cranes on her deck, each good for 30 metric tons, can lift cargo in and out of her holds.
Fednav once sailed her as the Federal Matane, before she took the name Lake Erie.
Her 2026 travels have taken her from Thunder Bay and Hamilton to Chicago's Calumet Harbor and all the way to Brazil.

vessels.name: CHAMPION
vessels.fact: Durocher Marine tug from Cheboygan, built in 1974
vessels.source: gltugs.wordpress.com/champion - built 1974 Amelia LA, 75 ft, 1,400 bhp, official number 556293, Durocher Marine of Cheboygan, contracting work. intelligence.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/champion-321061 - same USCG number, Durocher Marine, Great Lakes, built 1974, 1,400 hp (lists 63.7 ft register length). gltugs.wordpress.com/durocher-marine - current fleet, division of Kokosing. test.ipernity.com Joel Dinda tug photos - pushing barge Kokosing 2 in 2012. Other Champions ruled out: Campbell Transportation's 2013 tug is a Pittsburgh river boat.
facts: She works for Durocher Marine of Cheboygan, a neighbor just down the shore from the Straits of Mackinac.
Durocher, part of Kokosing Construction, is one of the largest marine contractors on the Great Lakes.
Built in Amelia, Louisiana, in 1974, she is 75 feet long with 1,400 horsepower.
She has been photographed pushing the company's work barge Kokosing 2, which is named for the parent company.
She goes wherever the job is, helping with construction and dredging projects around the Great Lakes.

vessels.name: ROBINSON BAY
vessels.fact: Seaway's old icebreaking tug, now a training boat for future mariners
vessels.source: tilife.org Thousand Islands Life, Workin' Robby Bay - nickname, 103 ft, Christy Corp., delivered April 1958, ice work between Eisenhower and Snell locks, about 200 navigation aids. gltugs.wordpress.com/robinson-bay - 1958, Christy Corp., 1991 repower and upper house, backup from 2020, transfer 2024. seawayreview.com/transfer-of-historic-robinson-bay-tugboat and marinelink.com/news/historic-tug-transferred-great-lakes-519602 - donated to Great Lakes Maritime Academy, over six decades of service.
facts: Christy Corporation of Sturgeon Bay built her for the St. Lawrence Seaway, which took delivery in April 1958.
Her crews nicknamed her Robby Bay, and she has been called the little tug that could.
Each spring she chopped ice into small pieces between the Eisenhower and Snell locks so ships could get through.
She tended about 200 buoys and markers on a stretch of more than 100 miles from Massena to Lake Ontario.
After six decades on the Seaway she was donated in 2024 to the Great Lakes Maritime Academy in Traverse City to train students.

vessels.name: THEO G
vessels.fact: Turkish-flagged ocean bulk carrier who visits the Great Lakes from overseas
vessels.source: maritimeoptima.com (IMO 9415246: type, 2009, Turkey, 185 m, also listed under the name THEA G); ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/271053634 (607 ft, 2026 calls at Hamilton and Montreal); magicport.ai (30,790 t deadweight, recent calls at Port Weller, Port Colborne, Milwaukee)
facts: She is a bulk carrier, built to carry loose cargo in her holds, and she stretches about 607 feet.
She can carry roughly 30,800 tonnes of cargo.
She is a true saltie: her 2026 log runs from Hamilton and Montreal to Italy, Ireland and Portugal.
Her recent Great Lakes stops include Port Weller, Port Colborne and Milwaukee.

vessels.name: RONNIE
vessels.fact: 482-foot heavy-lift saltie with two big cranes of her own
vessels.source: vesselfinder.com and magicport.ai (IMO 9736224: 2021, Antigua and Barbuda, 147 m, 12,325 t deadweight); ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/305434000 (482 ft, September 2026 calls at Montreal, Port Huron, Sarnia); marinelink.com German Shipowner Buys Two Multi-Purpose Vessels, Feb 2026 (Ernst Russ purchase, seven-year charter to dship Carriers, cranes); marinelink.com MV Charlie delivered article (four-ship F-500 class)
facts: She belongs to a family of four F-500 heavy-lift ships, alongside Mick, Keith and Charlie.
Two Liebherr cranes sit on her deck, and working together they can lift up to 500 tonnes.
Ernst Russ of Hamburg bought her in 2026, and she is on a seven-year charter to dship Carriers, a project cargo specialist.
In September 2026 she came up from Montreal and was logged at Port Huron and Sarnia.

vessels.name: MOLLY M 1
vessels.fact: McKeil Marine tug born in 1962, once the Foundation Vigour
vessels.source: mckeil.com/our-fleet/molly-m-i (McKeil project tug, Canadian flag, single screw); tugfaxblogspotcom.blogspot.com Nov 10 2014 post (built 1962, former names, 2006 sale to McKeil, Nadro operation, Halifax career); maritimeoptima.com and magicport.ai (IMO 5118838, 1962, Canada, AIS at Hamilton). Length left out because sources disagree.
facts: She started life in 1962 as Foundation Vigour, one of six sister tugs.
She later became Point Vigour and spent years as a harbor tug at Halifax, Nova Scotia.
McKeil's group bought her in 2006, and she took the name Molly M 1 the next year.
She is part of the project fleet of McKeil Marine, the Hamilton, Ontario towing company.
She has a single propeller, and it turns inside a nozzle that adds pulling power.

vessels.name: ECOSSE
vessels.fact: McKeil Marine project tug from 1979, twin screws and 1,500 horsepower
vessels.type: Great Lakes harbor and project tug
vessels.source: mckeil.com/our-fleet/ecosse (91 ft, 1,500 hp, twin screw, 14 t bollard pull, Canadian flag, project tug); maritimeoptima.com (IMO 8624682, 1979, Canada, recent calls at Montreal, Hamilton, Oswego); magicport.ai (McKeil Marine registered owner); globalmaritimehistory.com ship spotting post (built to support Lake Erie platforms, single source)
facts: She is a 91-foot tug in the fleet of McKeil Marine of Hamilton, Ontario.
Two propellers and 1,500 horsepower give her about 14 tonnes of pulling power.
McKeil uses her for harbor towing and for its project work.
Recent tracking shows her calling at Hamilton, Oswego and Montreal.

vessels.name: CHARLIE
vessels.fact: Fourth and final F-500 heavy-lift saltie, delivered in 2022
vessels.source: vesselfinder.com and magicport.ai (IMO 9736236: 2022, Antigua and Barbuda, 147 m); ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/305543000 (482 ft, October 2026 calls at Montreal, Port Weller, Burns Harbor); ajot.com dship Carriers launches MV Charlie (launched March 3 2021, cranes, 12,385 t deadweight, Becker devices, 75 m hold); marinelink.com MV Charlie delivered, Feb 2022 (fourth of four); marinelink.com Feb 2026 (Ernst Russ purchase and charter)
facts: She was launched in March 2021 and delivered in early 2022 as the fourth and final ship of her class.
Her two Liebherr cranes are each rated for 250 tons.
A special duct ahead of her propeller and a fin-fitted rudder help her save fuel.
Her class has a main hold about 75 meters long, with movable decks inside for odd-shaped cargo.
In October 2026 she went from Montreal through Port Weller to Burns Harbor, Indiana, on Lake Michigan.

vessels.name: BRUCE
vessels.fact: Liberian-flagged heavy-lift saltie, a 482-foot world traveler
vessels.source: vesselfinder.com, maritimeoptima.com and magicport.ai (IMO 9741140: 2016, Liberia, 147 m, 12,300 t deadweight, Burns Harbor call, Montreal next); ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/636093060 (482 ft, late 2026 calls at Port Weller and Burns Harbor, 2026 calls in Poland and Australia); ship-photos.de (Huanghai Shipyard builder, 2 x 250 t cranes, about 840 containers, single source)
facts: She was built in 2016 at the Huanghai Shipyard in Rongcheng, China.
She carries two 250-ton cranes on deck, handy for heavy project cargo.
She can hold about 840 standard containers or around 12,300 tonnes of cargo.
Her 2026 travels took her to Poland and Australia before she came up the Seaway.
In autumn 2026 she stopped at Port Weller and Burns Harbor, Indiana, then headed back toward Montreal.

vessels.name: STEELHEAD
vessels.fact: Michigan DNR research boat studying Lake Michigan fish from Charlevoix
vessels.source: content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/42d6a25 (DNR release: new 66 ft RV Steelhead, commissioned Sept 30 2026 at Charlevoix, surveys, features, named after old boat); content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/2e28521 (DNR profile of the 1968 boat: built at Escanaba, crew of five, Lakes Michigan and Huron); bairdmaritime.com Steelhead review (builder, solar, gyrostabilizer); wwmt.com (final testing on Lake Huron); michiganpublic.org (commissioning). Built and length left out because two boats share this name and AIS alone cannot tell which one passed.
facts: Steelhead is the name of the Michigan DNR boat that surveys Lake Michigan fish from Charlevoix.
A brand-new 66-foot Steelhead was commissioned at Charlevoix on September 30, 2026, taking over from an older boat of the same name built in 1968.
The new boat was built in Michigan by Moran Iron Works of Onaway, and she was tested on Lake Huron before delivery.
The new boat has a gyrostabilizer to keep her steady, a bow thruster and solar charging.
The original Steelhead was built at Escanaba, and a crew of five could live aboard her for weeklong trips.

vessels.name: COE LUISA
vessels.fact: 453-foot saltie who traveled from the ocean all the way to Duluth
vessels.source: shiphotos.com/Ship/?ID=29161 (IMO 9435026: builder, launch and commissioning dates, 138 m, 12,668 t deadweight, 15 knots, former names, COE Shipping fleet); ports.marinelink.com/vessels/vessel/305172000 (453 ft, October 2026 calls at Cleveland and Duluth-Superior); maritimeoptima.com (2008, Antigua and Barbuda, Thunder Bay, Duluth and Milwaukee calls); vesseltracker.com (flag, size)
facts: She was built in China and entered service in June 2008.
She has worn a few names: first Beluga Felicity, then BBC Tennessee, and now COE Luisa.
She has sailed in the fleet of COE Shipping of Buxtehude, Germany, since 2022.
She can carry about 12,700 tonnes and cruises at around 15 knots.
In autumn 2026 she made a grand Great Lakes tour with stops at Cleveland, Thunder Bay, Duluth-Superior and Milwaukee.
